title: Retention inheritance, impact preview, and forensics export for request data
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Goal: Provide a single, auditable model for retention across prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics that supports hierarchical inheritance (global -> region -> tenant -> route), an interactive impact preview for admins, and a compact forensics export bundle to satisfy audit requests. This ticket sculpts the product requirements for the UI/UX, API contract, and export packaging; separate engineering issues (ENG-2210 et al.) will implement runtime enforcement and background deletion jobs.
context: Current state: multiple retention features exist (per-route TTL, tenant-level defaults) but behavior is opaque to customers: no explainability for why a record will be retained or deleted, limited region-aware previews, and ad-hoc audit exports. Regulators and enterprise customers repeatedly ask for: 1) a preview of what data would remain if they shorten retention, 2) a single downloadable package with manifests and checksums for deleted/retained objects, and 3) clear precedence rules for conflicting policies across scopes.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce retention policy inheritance with precedence: explicit route policy > tenant policy > region override > global default. 2) Add an Impact Preview UI that simulates policy changes and shows estimated retained object counts, storage delta, and per-region residency implications for a selected time-window. 3) Implement a "Forensics Export" API that packages sample records, policy manifests, deletion job logs, and verification checksums into a signed archive for auditors. 4) Provide an API endpoint /console preview endpoints for programmatic simulation. 5) Add immutable audit record generation when policies change.
acceptance_criteria: Retention policy model defined and documented (precedence rules + inheritance semantics)
UI shows impact preview for a selected tenant+route for a configurable date range with estimated counts and storage impact
Preview simulation is conservative (never claims data will be deleted before actual deletion jobs run)
Forensics export returns a signed archive containing: policy-manifest.json, deletion-jobs-log.csv, sample-records (up to admin-specified limits), and verification.sha256
API endpoints exist for: GET /v1/retention/preview and POST /v1/retention/forensics-export with RBAC checks
Samples in export are scrubbed by default and include original residency metadata and retention decision rationale
Docs and admin help content published in console docs
End-to-end tests and a small load test for preview aggregation included
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Design sign-off and API contract (2 weeks). Phase 2: Backend aggregation and preview compute (ENG-2210) + minimal UI (alpha) behind feature flag for internal tenants (4 weeks). Phase 3: Forensics export implementation + security review (3 weeks). Phase 4: Gradual customer rollout and docs + webinar (2 weeks). Toggle: console feature flag per-tenant and opt-in export quota to limit heavy exports.
metrics: % of enterprise tenants using preview before retention change
number of support tickets related to retention surprises
successful verification checks in exported archives
risks: Preview accuracy: estimates may be off if background deletion lags; need conservative messaging
Performance: preview for large tenants may be expensive -> require sampling and cost limits
Security/privacy: exported samples must be scrubbed and signed to avoid data leaks
KMS key scope: when tenant uses customer-managed KMS, export packaging must not leak key material
Regulator requests for complete forensic sets may trigger heavy read jobs and legal review
qa_tests: Preview correctness tests with synthetic datasets (small/medium/large)
Forensics export contains all required manifests and verification file
RBAC and SSO test for export endpoints
Migration test: existing tenant defaults preserved

notes: Avoid claiming exact deletion times in UI. The preview is a planner tool; final deletion is performed by background jobs subject to maintenance windows and cross-region replication lag. Coordinate with Legal for export retention of forensics bundles.
design_feedback: Design prefers a three-column modal: left = policy tree, center = timeline + slider to change retention window, right = impact summary and per-region heatmap. Add 'what changed' diff view when applying new policy.
